ranking.note: Memory-safety hardening of the shared JSON parser outranks the feature-shaped P3s, so it leads the band rather than sitting mid-list.
Correctness of returned data (disk corruption reported as 'tx not found') is the category's top concern, so it moves well ahead of its score position.
Leaking unrelated MuSig2 keys/derivation paths into PSBTs is a data-correctness and privacy defect, ranked above pure feature additions.
Operators silently seeing 'Warnings: (none)' is a real wrong-output bug, placed above deferrable feature work.
Spurious 'Internal bug detected' for miners on shutdown is a concrete reported bug (#34262), ranked with the other bug fixes rather than low.
Useful but purely additive output for tooling; placed after the bug fixes in the same band.
Signed overflow that silently drops bans while reporting success is a genuine bug, so it rises above the documentation and test entries.
Conflicting progress numbers between two RPCs is a reporting bug, ranked with the other small correctness fixes.
Deprecation of a wallet RPC with migration cost for callers; valuable but deferrable, so it sits below the correctness fixes.
Opt-in management feature with no cited external requester; placed below the bug-fix cluster.
New observability RPC answering a feature request, ranked with the other requested additions rather than near the top.
Warning about silent key cloning has real user value, so it ranks above the purely cosmetic additions.
Diagnostic field with no external requester; per category rules new unrequested fields rank low.
RPC-side change is a refactor; its value is to GUI/IPC consumers outside this category.
Major project, but within rpc it only adapts internal dispatch structures and adds no user-facing RPC change.
Incremental diagnostic field in decodepsbt, but still more user-visible than the logging/test entries below it.
Logging-config RPC reshaping touches an administrative interface only; grouped with its two competing alternatives.
Competing alternative to #34038; grouped with it so the decision is taken once.
Largely a superset of #34038's logging RPC change plus an unmeasured hot-path optimization, so it trails both alternatives.
Band lowered: pure encapsulation refactor with no bug, performance, or interface effect, unlike #36159 which also fixes misleading logs and adds coverage.

inconsistencies: #34038, #35387 and #35355 are three overlapping reworks of -loglevel/the logging RPC: #34038 and #35387 are competing designs for the same problem and #35355 contains #34038's interface change plus atomics. Decide between #34038 and #35387 first; #35355 should not be reviewed as an independent interface change.
#34950 and #36384 do the same migration to self.Arg<>(); #36384 subsumes the generatetoaddress case, so review #36384 first and close #34950 as redundant if covered.
#36351 and #36266 both change dumptxoutset failure handling on pruned/assumeutxo nodes and will likely conflict; review #36351 (daemon abort) first, then #36266.

The post-libevent HTTP server cluster (#36355, #36259, #36354, #36204, #36200, #35780, #36303, #36124, #36159) all touch the same rewritten server from #35182; #36355 and #36259 both alter keep-alive/close bookkeeping, so #36355 should land first and #36259 be rebased on it. #36124 follows review feedback on already-merged #35829 and overlaps #36159's client code.
#35370 and #36332 both concern unwanted key-origin/MuSig2 metadata ending up in PSBTs; reviewing them together keeps the sanitisation semantics consistent.
#34534 (manual prune locks) and #36266 (dumptxoutset clobbering prune locks) touch the same prune-lock mechanism; #36266's fix should be settled before new user-facing lock RPCs are added.
#10102 depends on #29409 (not in this category) and in turn unblocks #19460/#19461; #33117's interface work targets the same multiprocess/GUI consumers.
result.notes: The band distribution is dominated by P3 because most of this list is additive RPC/REST surface. The clear separation is: three P1 interface-correctness/security items, a coherent P2 block of HTTP-server and REST defects around the libevent removal, and then a long P3 tail where bug fixes were ordered ahead of unrequested new fields and logging/test work.
